title: AutoFarm devlog: an AI-assisted pathfinding fix still needed another pass
author: jadkiar
selftext:
i'm making AutoFarm, a mouse-controlled idle farm manager in Godot. i use Claude and Codex for coding and review, and a recent pathfinding bug was a useful reminder to check the behavior in the game.



i wanted villagers to use the roads on their way to the market. after the first implementation, recording a gameplay clip showed that they were still cutting across the grass in a staircase pattern.



the road tiles had movement costs below 1, but the A\* estimate didn't account for that. the follow-up fix normalized the costs and used a Manhattan estimate for the grid without diagonals. a separate AI reviewer then caught that only one of two heuristic settings had been updated. that remaining setting was corrected too.



the checks compared routes on both maps with Dijkstra and got the same path cost. there's also a focused check that the market route actually uses the painted road. the clip here shows the resulting behavior.



my part was pointing out the unwanted behavior and deciding what the villagers should do. the agents implemented and reviewed the change. that separation helped, but the first generated fix still wasn't enough. what checks have helped you catch an AI-generated change that looks plausible in code but behaves wrong in-game?



AI disclosure: coding and review use AI assistants. the artwork mixes AI-generated images that i refine with asset packs. this post was prepared with AI assistance. the game is still in development, with no public demo or Steam page yet.
